chapters.title: Chapter 9: Capstone: Running a Market Making Book Through a Volatile Month

lessons.title: Week Two: A Volatility Shock and the Full Toolkit in Action

body.text: Every limit set before the month began, and every baseline number from week one, exists for exactly this week. This is the week that actually tests them.

children.text: Unlike week one's calendar-scheduled data release, Tuesday's shock arrives with no warning: an unexpected risk-off macro headline hits the tape, and Bank Nifty starts falling. Put buying turns sharply one-sided within minutes, hitting the desk's ask again and again, exactly the pattern Chapter 3 first described. Inventory, which had been sitting near flat all morning, starts climbing fast, and by 11:45am it has already reached 180 units, well past anything the book has seen since week one began.
The Toolkit Engages: Skewing, Size Adjustment, and VPIN

The desk's reservation price shifts above the mid as its short exposure builds, exactly as Chapter 3's Avellaneda-Stoikov lesson described, pushing both bid and ask upward to make selling puts back to the desk more attractive and buying more of them less so. On the specific strikes where the tick genuinely constrains further price movement, the desk falls back to size skewing from Chapter 3's third lesson, posting less size on the side that keeps adding to its short. At the same time, VPIN readings on this contract climb sharply, confirming this is not a brief overreaction but genuinely toxic, one-sided flow, which is exactly the kind of real-time signal Chapter 4's third lesson was built to provide.

By 12:15pm, inventory has reached 280 units, close to the 300-unit maximum set in this capstone's first lesson, and the session's running loss has reached ₹1.3 lakh, uncomfortably close to the ₹1.5 lakh kill switch threshold from that same setup. Skewing has been slowing the buildup, but not reversing it fast enough. The desk faces the exact choice from Chapter 3's third lesson: keep skewing and hope flow turns, or pay to unwind now, before the kill switch potentially forces an uglier, uncontrolled halt.
The Decision: A Deliberate Unwind Before the Kill Switch Forces One

The desk chooses to act before its own limits force the decision for it. It sends a series of Immediate-or-Cancel orders, from Chapter 5's first lesson, to buy back 150 units cleanly with no resting exposure left behind, and works the remainder through an iceberg order to avoid signalling the full size of its remaining unwind to the rest of the market. Inventory falls to 130 units within minutes, and the session's running loss stabilises at ₹95,000, a real cost, but comfortably inside the ₹1.5 lakh kill switch and nowhere near the month's ₹5 lakh pause threshold. The rest of the afternoon is spent skewing the residual position down further through ordinary flow, ending the session at 40 units.

body.title: Reading Week Two Through Chapter 6's Lens
body.scenario: A colleague sees week two's numbers, a much lower spread capture rate, a higher fill ratio, longer holding time, and a slightly negative week overall, and worries this proves the desk never really had an edge to begin with.
body.prompt: Using Chapter 6's case study on telling a genuine edge from a lucky quarter, is this worry justified? What in week two's numbers would actually distinguish a genuine edge under stress from no edge at all?
body.modelAnswer: The worry is not well justified based on these numbers. Chapter 6's case study specifically identified what would indicate no real edge: spread capture rate collapsing to near zero or negative, and losses breaching the desk's own hard limits. Neither happened here: spread capture rate fell hard but stayed positive at 52%, well above zero, the worst single-session loss of ₹95,000 stayed clearly inside the ₹1.5 lakh kill switch, and the week finished only modestly negative rather than catastrophically so. This pattern, metrics deteriorating under real stress but staying within bounds and remaining directionally sound, is much closer to Chapter 6's description of a genuine, if imperfect, edge than to a book with no edge at all.

body.title: Why the Desk Unwound Before the Kill Switch Triggered
body.question: Why did the desk choose to execute a partial unwind at 12:15pm rather than simply continuing to skew until either flow reversed or the kill switch triggered on its own?
options: Because skewing alone had already completely failed to slow the buildup
Because acting deliberately, before a hard limit forces an uncontrolled halt, is the disciplined escalation pattern from Chapter 3, rather than waiting passively for the worst case
Because IOC orders are always required by SEBI once inventory exceeds 250 units
Because the kill switch had already triggered by 12:15pm
body.explanation: Skewing had been working, just not fast enough relative to how close the book was getting to its own limits. Chapter 3's escalation logic specifically favours a deliberate, chosen unwind over waiting for a hard limit to force an uncontrolled one, which is exactly the choice the desk made here, well before the kill switch itself was actually triggered.

points: Week two's unscheduled shock tested nearly every tool this course has covered in a single morning: reservation price skewing, size skewing under a tick constraint, VPIN confirmation, and a deliberate IOC-and-iceberg unwind
The desk came close to, but stayed inside, both its single-session kill switch and its month-level drawdown pause, exactly the layered protection built into the setup in this capstone's first lesson
Spread capture rate falling to 52% while staying clearly positive, alongside a contained worst-case loss, is consistent with a genuine edge under real stress, not with an edge that never existed

Choosing to unwind deliberately before a hard limit forces an uncontrolled halt is the same disciplined escalation pattern taught in Chapter 3, now applied under real pressure within this capstone's own story
Week two's numbers, worse than week one's but still fundamentally sound, are exactly the kind of evidence Chapter 6 said actually matters for judging a book's edge
The final lesson reviews the full month, brings every metric together, and asks what should actually change going into month two
